title: Spec graph
no_project: Open a project to see its spec findings.
now_hint: Every deterministic finding at the project's branch: traceability, links and anchors, superseded decisions, the repository's own rules. These may gate a pull request.
stored_hint: What the project's runs stored in its graph: contradictions the judges confirmed, with both passages, and the other judges' findings. A model's judgment: advisory until its rule is calibrated.
setup_title: Set the project up for the spec graph
setup_hint: The spec-graph service reads the project's first Git source through Studio's Git proxy, at its branch. Say which documents: gear directories (gears/a gears/b), or every Markdown file under one directory (--docs-root docs --name LABEL .).
pulls_hint: Review an open pull request as the spec-graph CI does: the findings it brings (its head against the base below) and the threads CI would post. Review is the deterministic rules, in seconds; With model adds the model's rules (contradictions), minutes and model cost.
no_pulls: No open pull requests in {repository} (as Studio last synced them).
pulls_no_repository: The repository this graph reads is not among the project's sources any more, so its pull requests cannot be told apart from other repositories'. Set the project up again.
pulls_other_repos: Pull requests of the project's other repositories are not listed ({count}): this graph reads {repository} only.
reviewing_model: Reviewing with the model: a run of a few minutes…
review_hint: Studio does not post these on the pull request yet: they are what CI posts, one thread per rule and lines.
review_clean: The pull request brings no finding.
graph_view_hint: The project's spec graph around one node: what points at it on the left, what it points at on the right, a judge's conclusion as a dashed line. Choose a neighbour to centre on it.
graph_hint: Find a node (a requirement, a section, a decision), or open one from a finding with Show in graph.
graph_legend: Left: what points at this node. Right: what it points at. Solid: stated in the documents. Dashed: a judge's conclusion.
